documentation: Every corvidae workspace's disposition when the mirror transform emits a public target, plus a ruling on each name that is published (or was once reserved) without corvidae source. The transform hard-errors on any workspace absent from `workspaces`; it never silently skips one. `publish-as` carries the public npm name, and is the only disposition that puts anything on the registry. `private-workspace` ships to the mirror repository but never into a tarball. `exclude` is not emitted at all. Names under `publishedOnly` have no corvidae source, so no sync can maintain them: `keep` means a human maintains it elsewhere, `deprecate` means publish a deprecation notice, and `orphan-untouched` means leave the registry entry exactly as it is.

@corvidae/weft.name: @lostgradient/weft
@corvidae/weft.reason: Already published under this name. Ships standalone from stevekinney/weft.

@corvidae/weft-ui.name: @lostgradient/weft-ui
@corvidae/weft-ui.reason: Name is settled, but `npm view @lostgradient/weft-ui` returns 404 — the manifest carries 0.1.0 and no `private` flag, yet it was never published. COR-1194 records that its trusted-publisher registration was never completed. Treat the first monorepo release as a first publish, not a re-publish.

@corvidae/cinder.name: @lostgradient/cinder
@corvidae/cinder.reason: Already published under this name. Its exports map is regenerated by the transform per COR-1186, not copied.

@corvidae/armorer.name: armorer
@corvidae/armorer.reason: Keeps its unscoped name deliberately. Roughly 30,872 installs a month; renaming breaks real consumers for a cosmetic gain.

@corvidae/conversationalist.name: conversationalist
@corvidae/conversationalist.reason: Keeps its unscoped name deliberately. Roughly 53,608 installs a month, the most-installed package in the graph.

@corvidae/cryptography.name: @lostgradient/cryptography
@corvidae/cryptography.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of published armorer and operative, so it must publish or those packages are uninstallable. Never published before. The unscoped name `cryptography` belongs to an unrelated third party (jnssnmrcs, 1.2.3, 2018) and is unavailable. Scoped name approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@corvidae/embeddings.name: @lostgradient/embeddings
@corvidae/embeddings.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of published armorer and operative. Never published before. The unscoped name `embeddings` belongs to an unrelated third party (pagepixels, 2.0.5, 2023) and is unavailable. Scoped name approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@corvidae/tool-protocol.name: @lostgradient/tool-protocol
@corvidae/tool-protocol.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of four published packages. Never published before. The unscoped name `tool-protocol` is genuinely unregistered, but the scoped name was chosen for consistency with its siblings and approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@corvidae/lifecycle.name: @lostgradient/lifecycle
@corvidae/lifecycle.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of four published packages, reached both directly and through tool-protocol. Never published — agent-bureau's manifest is `private: true` at 0.0.1. The unscoped name `lifecycle` belongs to an unrelated third party (kmalakoff, 1.0.4, 2015) and is unavailable. Scoped name approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@corvidae/typescript.reason: Every published package extends it, but only through devDependencies — it appears in no runtime `dependencies` edge anywhere. Must remain in the repository because dropping it breaks typecheck and build for every workspace. COR-1189 vendors it to a local path for the single-package weft target and keeps it workspace-native for the monorepo.

@corvidae/testing.reason: Test infrastructure imported from 505 test files and 26 non-test files, all of which are harnesses, fixture loaders, and scripts. Never in a runtime dependencies edge. COR-1196 states this disposition explicitly: it ships to the mirror repository but never into a tarball.

@corvidae/chat-room.reason: A deployable application rather than a library. No workspace declares it as a dependency.

@corvidae/bureau.reason: Not reachable in any published package's runtime closure, so publishing is genuinely optional and declining breaks nobody. Never published — agent-bureau's manifest is `private: true` at 0.0.8, and the unscoped name `bureau` belongs to an unrelated third party (merrihew, 0.0.0, 2014). Left private as the reversible default; `@lostgradient/bureau` is unregistered and available if this is revisited.

@corvidae/memory.reason: Not reachable in any published package's runtime closure. Never published — `private: true` at 0.0.1, and the unscoped name `memory` belongs to an unrelated third party (edwardhotchkiss, 0.0.3, 2011). Left private as the reversible default; `@lostgradient/memory` is unregistered and available.

@corvidae/skills.reason: Not reachable in any published package's runtime closure. Never published — `private: true` at 0.0.1. The unscoped name `skills` is Vercel Labs' actively maintained package (1.7.0, modified 2026-09-17) and is categorically unavailable. Left private as the reversible default; `@lostgradient/skills` is unregistered and available.

publishedOnly.policy: Names with no corvidae source. A sync can never maintain these, so each needs an explicit ruling rather than silence. `deprecate` is permanently public and requires the repository owner's approval; none is currently set.

entries.name: @lostgradient/cinder-mcp
entries.reason: Public with provenance, but it has no corvidae source, so no sync can maintain it. Leaving the registry entry exactly as it is breaks no consumer, whereas deprecating it is a permanently public act. Revisit deliberately rather than as a migration side effect.

entries.name: cloudflare
entries.reason: Private in the upstream repository and never published. Nothing to keep or deprecate.

entries.name: evaluation
entries.reason: Private in the upstream repository and never published.

entries.name: gateway
entries.reason: Private in the upstream repository and never published.

entries.name: integration
entries.reason: Private in the upstream repository and never published.

entries.name: @cinder/playground
entries.reason: Private and never published. Moves into corvidae as an application in COR-1200, at which point it becomes a workspace and leaves this list.

entries.name: interoperability
entries.reason: Private and never published. Deleted by corvidae's consolidation.

entries.name: @cinder/testing
entries.reason: The `@cinder/*` scope stops matching anything once stevekinney/cinder is renamed in COR-1193. This name corresponds to @corvidae/testing, which is a private workspace, so the scope change breaks no consumer.

entries.name: @cinder/chat-room-lab
entries.reason: Private and never published. The labs chat-room deployment is explicitly out of this project's scope and follows its own disposition.

openQuestions: @corvidae/bureau, @corvidae/memory, and @corvidae/skills are set to private-workspace as the reversible default rather than a positive decision to keep them unpublished. Each has an available @lostgradient/* name if that changes.

@lostgradient/cinder-mcp is left untouched rather than deprecated. It has no corvidae source and therefore no maintenance path through this pipeline; whether it should be deprecated, re-homed, or given source is unresolved.

COR-1189's surface-parity gate fetches each published package's last subpath set from the registry. The four packages newly marked publish-as here have no published predecessor, so that gate has no baseline for them and must treat a missing predecessor as a first publish rather than a parity failure.
